Review reference: owner decision 25 of 2026-11-01 (D-Eminence, in chat), "all recommended except D5", on the Akos handover backend plan, items 3b and 4 (Akos plan step 4; D6: no drug picture until the price list; D9: the quantity to dispense is the prescriber's suggestion, the pharmacist confirms it and nothing compares the two). NUMBER AND ORDER: the plan's 0107 was numbered 0114 (coordinator's numbering of 3 Nov 2026) and released jointly with 0113; by the coordinator's release order of 11 Nov 2026 it was 0122, shipping on its own after 0121 (the own-work patient cards, #160, formerly 0113), and it is now 0125: staging took 0117-0121 (0117 recorded allergies, 0118-0121 outreach), then 0122 (the Access PIN port) and 0123 (the sealed QA tenant), signed by the owner and merged from #253 into staging e50ac518 on 17 Nov 2026, and #160 is now 0124, which has its own declaration. This declaration therefore lists only 0125 and runtime-grants.sql, and assumes production has applied 0124; if it has not, the release stops with EXACT_SCHEMA_CHANGE_DECLARATION_REQUIRED (or the declaration must be widened to 0124, 0125 and runtime-grants.sql). 0125 uses nothing 0124 adds and relies on no body 0124 creates. It needs 0001-0124 applied (0124 needs 0001-0123) and relies on one body 0104 replaced, the read consent test identity.has_active_consent_grant as 0104 left it (0108 and 0117-0124 kept it), which the work items' read policy calls too, and uses nothing else 0104-0124 add. Of 0112-0124, two replace a body it pins, and it accepts both bodies of each: 0112 (OCR source deletion) replaces ehr.capture_record_version, which keeps 0004's behaviour for every call but its own purge, and 0125 accepts 0004's body (md5 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702) or 0112's (cae99883d00e70ab1d20ed6fbc97ad7b); 0123 (the sealed QA tenant) replaces ehr.send_order_route, and 0125 accepts 0098's body (4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c) or 0123's (0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b). Any other body of either is refused. Staging's 0113-0122 change none of the bodies or objects it pins, and 0123 changes one: on a database built by staging e50ac518's own runner (0001-0123) every pinned md5 is the one 0125 expects (the same values as on staging 91e9fb0a and 40ea031a; ehr.capture_record_version is 0112's body), except that ehr.send_order_route has 0123's body, which 0125 now accepts; the attributes of the eight functions, the three triggers on ehr.prescriptions, the two read policies, work_items_route_facility_ck, the snapshot key, forced row-level security on both tables and the 18 columns read are also as expected. No other pin changed in the port or after 0122 and 0123. 0117 (recorded allergies) adds a foreign key from ehr.prescription_allergy_acknowledgements to ehr.prescriptions; its two action triggers on ehr.prescriptions are internal ones, which the trigger check leaves out, and it adds no trigger, policy or column there. Of the two migrations released before it (#253, on staging e50ac518), 0122 (the Access PIN) replaces identity.access_patient_with_pin and redefines the PIN scope CHECKs on identity.access_requests and identity.consent_grants, identity_outbox_minimum_necessary and the outbox's PIN insert policy, none of which 0125 pins; 0123 (the sealed QA tenant) adds the QA seal's tables, functions and triggers on identity tables, changes the patients_registration_read policy and replaces eleven functions, of which 0125 pins only ehr.send_order_route (0098's body 4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c), now md5 0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b. That was this declaration's open point (resolved): with that body live on staging 91e9fb0a, the previous 0125 file's dry run stopped at its precondition (0125: an object this migration relies on differs from 0001-0121: ehr.send_order_route(uuid,text,uuid,uuid,uuid,bigint,uuid,text,text,character) md5 0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b), with nothing applied. 0123's body is 0098's with one clause added: the receiving-facility check that answers ORDER_ROUTE_DESTINATION_INELIGIBLE also refuses a facility on the other side of the QA seal, beside the demo seal. The two bodies differ in that line only; the declarations (prescription_order ehr.prescriptions%ROWTYPE among them), the read of the prescription FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the replay read of its version and status and the UPDATE of its status alone are byte for byte 0098's, so 0123 changes nothing 0125 relies on. 0125 therefore accepts 0123's body as well as 0098's, as it accepts 0112's snapshot writer beside 0004's, in its precondition (section 0), its post-check (section 5) and its suite, and refuses any other body. runtime-grants.sql here holds staging's file (with its 0117-0121 and 0123 blocks), then 0124's block, then 0125's (EXECUTE on the Pharmacy details reader). Its base is now staging e50ac518 (0001-0123, 124 files, with 0122 and 0123 signed and merged from #253) plus 0124 (aadb566c, which merged staging e50ac518). WHAT CHANGES. ehr.prescriptions gains seven nullable columns without default, so no rewrite and every existing row reads null: priority, medication_strength, medication_dose_form, duration_value integer, duration_unit, quantity_to_dispense numeric(12,4) and quantity_unit (the others text), and one CHECK, prescriptions_dispensing_details_ck, added NOT VALID and then validated, so the table is scanned once: priority routine, urgent, asap or stat; medication_strength and quantity_unit not blank and at most 80 characters; medication_dose_form tablet, capsule, liquid, injection, cream, inhaler, drops or other; duration_value 1-3650 and duration_unit day, week or month, both or neither; quantity_to_dispense above 0 and quantity_unit, both or neither (one CHECK for the seven columns, not one per rule, because each VALIDATE CONSTRAINT scans the whole table under the lock; the EHR API checks each rule by name before it writes). One new function, pharmacy.work_item_prescription_details(uuid[]) (md5 e6013d732354a56794ad8ec7f2bbaf0c), plpgsql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name qualified), owned by pharmacy.work_items' owner, no migration number in its body. For each given work item that is own work (order_route_id null) at the session's facility, whose member holds pharmacy.work-item.read there (auth.membership_has_permission) and passes identity.has_active_consent_grant(patient, subject, membership, facility, 'read_records', the session's purpose), the own-row branch of the work items' read policy (so an emergency session with an active break-glass grant is included, and a revoked, expired or held grant, a deny directive, an inactive membership or a disabled account gives no row), it answers the seven values of the prescription version Pharmacy accepted, read from that version's snapshot in ehr.record_versions (resource_type 'prescriptions', resource_id the prescription id, version_no the accepted version, naming the work item's patient, facility and encounter), so they stay those of the accepted version after the prescription changes. The work item's keys are turned into text in a materialized CTE before the join, so the join compares text with text (texteq is leakproof) and uses the snapshot key (resource_type, resource_id, version_no) under the forced read policy, which then runs once per work item; a join on the uuid cast to text inside it (uuid_out is not leakproof) cannot be an index condition below the policy, which then ran on every prescription snapshot of the item's patient or facility. At most 200 ids, else 22023 WORK_ITEM_PRESCRIPTION_DETAILS_INVALID. The snapshot path was decided by test: ehr.record_versions' only read policy is ehr.context_allows(patient_id, facility_id, 'read_records'), the same facility-and-consent test for an own row, and under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner the suite reads every expected value through it. Nothing is copied into pharmacy.work_items: pharmacy.validate_work_item (0100, e2411539ee8c95a02dad46c03e24db05), pharmacy.validate_dispensing (0101, 17f7e8897bd2ab240332e4d2c9f757b7), ehr.send_order_route (0098's body 4202ba3bbf02abd7db34606d42adca9c, or 0123's 0c2def2b530bcb3d68537ade52787b6b once 0123 is live), ehr.sync_order_routes_on_order_change (0086, 8ce6b42450cc06fc02fec8d1cf63af41) and ehr.capture_record_version (0004's body 70daa16f05bb3ec28f05292e6358a702, or 0112's cae99883d00e70ab1d20ed6fbc97ad7b once 0112 is live) are untouched and checked before and after. No policy, trigger, index, role or other function changes; no existing row is touched. runtime-grants.sql gains a 0125 block: EXECUTE to hid_pharmacy_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, revoked from PUBLIC; the migration grants exactly the same; the EHR runtime's privileges on ehr.prescriptions are table-wide and cover the new columns. SERVICES: each behind PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED, new in ehr-api and in pharmacy-api, off by default (infra/aws, which is not the production source, passes it to both from HID_PRESCRIPTION_DISPENSING_DETAILS_ENABLED at synth, false unless that is true; it switches both at once, so it is set only after 0125 is applied, as below). Off, ehr-api validates the create body against today's CreatePrescriptionDto with the options main.ts installs (now one shared factory), so a new field answers today's 400 VALIDATION_FAILED word for word (jest, over HTTP, against a route declared as before), no statement names the new columns and no answer or list carries a new key; pharmacy-api sends no new statement and answers exactly as before (jest). On, POST .../prescriptions takes the seven as optional, create-only fields (pairs enforced: 400 DURATION_INCOMPLETE or QUANTITY_INCOMPLETE), every prescription answer echoes the ones set, the list says dispensingDetails: true, and a body without them keeps its Idempotency-Key digest (absent DTO fields are own undefined properties, which the digest prints, so the new ones are left out when absent and a retry across the deploy replays); pharmacy-api adds priority, medication.strength, medication.doseForm, duration (else the whole days from the work item's own start date to its end date, when both are set) and quantityToDispense with quantityUnit to own rows of the work list and of a work item, read in a savepoint (a failure leaves out the prescriber's values; the duration from the work item's own dates stays); route-backed rows and the acceptance answer are unchanged and no audit row is added. Today's images on the new schema answer as before: every writer and reader of ehr.prescriptions names its columns, and the bodies that read the row into ehr.prescriptions%ROWTYPE re-resolve after ADD COLUMN, also in a pooled connection that ran them before (proved: one psql session ran the pharmacy-prescription-source, pharmacy-dispensing-source and order-routes-send suites on 0103 + 0113, the runner applied 0114 (now 0125) from another connection, and the same session ran them and the 0125 suite again, all passing; the 0125 suite also adds a further column in its own session and accepts, dispenses and reads again). Switch the ehr-api setting on only after 0125 is applied, and off before restoring ehr-api's database to a point before 0125 or pointing ehr-api at a database without it: while it is on without the seven columns every prescription statement names them and fails (42703), so every prescription route of ehr-api answers 500; pharmacy-api only leaves the prescriber's values out (savepoint). Cost while the pharmacy-api setting is on: each list load calls the reader once for its own rows (at most 200), a statement of its own, under pharmacy-api's 15 s statement limit; under a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner each row pays the work items' read policy, the same consent test again and the snapshot table's read policy, once each (pg_stat_user_functions: 200 snapshot-policy calls for 200 items): 1.0-1.7 s for 200 own rows, against 0.4-0.7 s for reading the same rows under row-level security, with 1, 5, 20 or 50 prescription snapshots per patient and with 300,000 other snapshots at the facility (fictional data, a shared 4-CPU machine). The first draft's join on the uuid cast to text took 3.5 s with 5 and 8.8 s with 20 snapshots per patient (4,000 snapshot-policy calls for 200 items), and stopped at the 15 s limit with 1 per patient beside 100,000 other prescription snapshots, so the details would have been dropped; the answers of both bodies were identical wherever both finished.
